messages:
anya: Heads-up — seeing a persistent tailstorm on pool-dedicated-us-west starting ~08:40 UTC, p95 token latency jumped ~3x
mike: ugh saw the alert too. quick glance: kernel_select fallback to reference kernels at 08:39, KV cache hit-rate dropped from 92% -> 58% on that pool :grimacing:
julia: did the route-level traffic pattern change? any sudden large-context requests?
mike: per-route KPI shows /chat/compose had a batch of long seq (>=2048) from a single customer, ~1k requests in 3m window
anya: that matches the KV eviction logs — evictions spiked when that customer ramped. batching heuristics tried to coalesce and increased batch size -> longer queuing for short requests
ryan: noisy-neighbor sigs: GPU load stable, but queue_time variance per worker high. proposing per-route batching caps + adaptive KV reserve for hot prefixes
ops-oncall: forwarded incident to on-call infra. migrating some traffic off the pool to reduce headroom pressure.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-6821 | pool-dedicated-us-west tail latency regression | severity=high | assignees=@anya,@mike
anya: quick profiling dump attached in #eng-runtime, but here's the hot-spot: kernel_selector::pick() falling back due to "unsupported_seq_len_for_quant_kernels" check
mike: here's a small repro of the issue — when seq_len >=2048 AND model_variant == quant_f16 the kernel chooser falls back. snippet:
```
if (seq_len > KERNEL_MAX || !kernel_supported(variant)) {
  use_reference_kernel();
}
```

mike: reference kernel lacks the continuous-batching optimizations so per-token cost spikes and KV lookups pile up
julia: ops question: can we fast-fail batching for routes with >95% short-context historically? prevent them from waiting on long-context coalescing
anya: yes, we have per-route batching caps feature but it's not enabled for /chat/compose (legacy route)

ryan: quick mitigation plan suggested in thread: 1) enable per-route max_batch=32 for /chat/compose 2) temporarily pin that route to a different pool with reserved KV memory 3) add a kernel capability flag to avoid fallback when quant kernel can handle that seq_len but with reduced perf
ops-oncall: executing step 2 now — shifting 12% of route traffic to pool-dedicated-us-east. will monitor headroom
sre-bot: Deploy Bot: rolling config change to /chat/compose max_batch=32 in 30s...
mike: after the rollout, KV hit-rate for pool-dedicated-us-west recovered from 58% -> 86% in 5m, p95 token latency back to baseline
anya: nice. follow-ups: - add metric for kernel_fallback_reason (enum) to token-level latency breakdowns - instrument batch composition (fractions of short vs long seq) - dashboard panel showing per-pool KV reserve vs eviction rate
ryan: also propose a short-term dashboard alert: if per-pool avg_batch_size increases >2x and KV hit-rate drops >15% in 5m, fire a noisy-neighbor signal and recommend traffic split
julia: can we add a synthetic probe that emits prefix-heavy requests to measure KV pressure before customer traffic does?
mike: yes, we already have a loadtest job we can tweak to run prefix-heavy probes as part of canary runs
anya: creating a GH issue for the kernel capability flag + dashboard panels. pinging @eng-runtime for PRs on kernel_selector and @eng-platform for dashboard work
ops-oncall: incident resolved for now. leaving monitoring open for 2 hours. :white_check_mark:
ryan: thanks all. will follow up with a short postmortem + runbook additions about per-route batching caps and KV reservation guidance
julia: add me to the postmortem, will draft the dashboard change request
mike: saved relevant flamegraphs and perf traces under s3://redwood-perf/1745006789/ for the postmortem
anya: excellent. TL;DR: long-context coalescing + quant kernel fallback -> reference kernel -> higher per-token latency -> KV pressure -> noisy-neighbor-like headroom exhaustion. Mitigated by per-route max_batch and traffic split. Follow-ups logged. :memo:
